name: Jason
kicker: Leader of the Argonauts · Sailed the Argo for the Golden Fleece
briefing: Jason was a Greek hero whose scheming uncle Pelias sent him on what looked like an impossible quest: sail to the edge of the known world and steal the Golden Fleece. He recruited the greatest heroes in Greece, including Heracles and the musician Orpheus, to crew his ship, the _Argo_. He only pulled it off with help from the clever sorceress Medea, whom he later betrayed, with tragic results for them both.

sample.note: 10 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (4 Middle School/Easy High School + 6 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: As an infant, this man was secretly raised by the centaur Chiron after his uncle seized his father’s throne in Iolcus. Years later, the craftsman Argus built this man a fifty-oared ship with help from the goddess Athena, who fitted its prow with a piece of prophetic oak from Zeus’s grove at Dodona.
tossups.r: Orpheus once drowned out the deadly song of the Sirens with his lyre to protect this man’s crew. For 10 points, name this captain of the Argo who led the Argonauts on the quest for the Golden Fleece.

tossups.p: This man arrived in Iolcus wearing only one sandal, having lost the other crossing a river, which alarmed his uncle when an old prophecy was recalled. On the island of Lemnos, this man and his crew were welcomed by Queen Hypsipyle and her husbandless subjects.
tossups.r: This man’s crew later drove off the Harpies tormenting the blind prophet Phineus, who repaid them with directions to Colchis. For 10 points, name this leader of the Argonauts, who sought the Golden Fleece.

tossups.p: This man’s ship passed safely through the crashing Symplegades [“sim-pleh-GAH-deez”], or Clashing Rocks, after its crew sent a dove through the gap first. At Colchis, King Aeetes told this man that he could only have the Golden Fleece if he could yoke a pair of fire-breathing bronze bulls and plow a field with them.
tossups.r: He then sowed a dragon’s teeth into that same field and watched armed warriors spring up from the furrows. For 10 points, name this hero who led the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece.

tossups.p: This man defeated the warriors who sprouted from a dragon’s teeth he had sown by tossing a rock into their ranks, tricking them into killing each other. The Fleece itself hung in a sacred grove guarded by a dragon that never slept, until this man’s companion sang it into slumber.
tossups.r: That companion was the sorceress Medea, who helped this man steal the Fleece and later became his wife. For 10 points, name this captain of the Argo and leader of the Argonauts.

tossups.p: Fleeing Colchis with the stolen Fleece, this man’s new wife killed her own brother, Apsyrtus, to slow down their pursuers. Earlier on the voyage, this man’s crewmate Heracles had been left behind while searching for his companion Hylas, who was pulled into a spring by water nymphs.
tossups.r: This man’s ship, built by Argus with Athena’s help, carried a speaking plank cut from an oak at Dodona. For 10 points, name this Greek hero who led the Argonauts on the quest for the Golden Fleece.

tossups.p: Back in Iolcus, this man’s wife tricked the daughters of his wicked uncle Pelias into trying a deadly spell on their own father, falsely promising that the magic that made an old ram young again would work on him too. That trick killed Pelias instead.
tossups.r: This man and his wife, Medea, were then exiled to Corinth. For 10 points, name this hero who had led the Argonauts in the quest for the Golden Fleece before his uncle’s death.

tossups.p: Years after returning from Colchis, this man abandoned his sorceress wife to marry Glauce, a princess of Corinth also called Creusa. His jilted wife sent the new bride a cursed golden robe and crown as a wedding gift, which burned her to death.
tossups.r: That same wife, Medea, then killed the two sons she had with this man, as revenge for his betrayal, before escaping in a chariot lent by her grandfather, the sun god Helios. For 10 points, name this hero and former leader of the Argonauts.

tossups.p: This man’s uncle had seized the throne of Iolcus from this man’s father and then sent this man on a near-impossible quest, hoping he would never return. On the way to complete it, this man’s crew rescued the blind seer Phineus from a flock of Harpies that kept stealing his food.
tossups.r: Phineus then told this man how to sail the Argo through the Clashing Rocks. For 10 points, name this nephew of King Pelias who led the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece.

tossups.p: This man’s crew included the only woman among the Argonauts, the huntress Atalanta, as well as the twins Castor and Pollux. This man completed deadly trials set by King Aeetes of Colchis, including yoking bulls that breathed fire, with help from the king’s daughter.
tossups.r: That princess, the sorceress Medea, helped him defeat an army sprung from dragon’s teeth. For 10 points, name this captain of the Argo who sought the Golden Fleece to reclaim his throne from Pelias.

tossups.p: According to one legend, this man founded the city of Ljubljana after slaying a dragon there on his way home from his most famous voyage. In another tale, this man’s half-rotten ship later collapsed and killed him while he rested in its shade.
tossups.r: Earlier, Orpheus’s music had saved this man’s crew from the Sirens. For 10 points, name this Greek hero who commanded the Argo and its crew of Argonauts on the quest for the Golden Fleece.

tossups.p: This man’s father-in-law, King Aeetes of Colchis, demanded that he plow a field with bronze oxen that breathed fire before he could take a certain treasure. A potion from this man’s future wife protected him from the oxen’s fiery breath before he sowed a dragon’s teeth like seeds.
tossups.r: Those teeth grew into warriors that this man defeated by throwing a single stone among them. For 10 points, name this leader of the Argonauts who sought the Golden Fleece with help from Medea.

tossups.p: This man’s crew once camped on the all-female island of Lemnos, where he fathered twins with its queen before his companions urged him to continue the voyage. Later, this man’s ship squeezed through the Symplegades, narrowly avoiding being crushed between two moving rocks.
tossups.r: This man then faced trials set by King Aeetes to win the Golden Fleece, with help from the king’s daughter, Medea. For 10 points, name this captain of the Argo who led the Argonauts.

tossups.p: This man’s uncle, Pelias, had promised to give up the throne of Iolcus if this man could bring back a certain golden-wooled treasure from the far-off kingdom of Colchis. Along the way, this man’s crew lost the strongman Heracles, who stayed behind searching for a lost companion.
tossups.r: At Colchis, this man won the help of the sorceress Medea to complete his quest. For 10 points, name this hero who led the Argonauts in their search for the Golden Fleece.

tossups.p: On the way home, this man’s ship slipped past the monster Scylla and a deadly whirlpool with help from the sea nymph Thetis. Earlier, this man had agreed to let his new wife murder her own brother, Apsyrtus, during their escape from Colchis.
tossups.r: That marriage ended badly years later in Corinth. For 10 points, name this Greek hero and captain of the Argo who led the Argonauts on the quest for the Golden Fleece.

tossups.p: This man wore only one sandal when he first arrived at his uncle’s court, fulfilling a prophecy that unsettled King Pelias. Before that, this man had been trained in secret by the wise centaur Chiron, far from Iolcus.
tossups.r: Pelias then sent this man to distant Colchis to fetch the Golden Fleece, never expecting him to survive. For 10 points, name this hero who led the Argonauts and later married the sorceress Medea.

clues.t: Captain of the ship _Argo_ and leader of the band of heroes called the Argonauts
Sent on a quest to find and bring back the Golden Fleece
Married the sorceress Medea, who helped him on his quest and whom he later betrayed
Sent on the quest by his scheming uncle, King Pelias, who had seized the throne of Iolcus
Arrived in Iolcus wearing only one sandal, a bad omen that worried Pelias
At Colchis, King Aeetes made him yoke a pair of fire-breathing bronze bulls and plow a field
Sowed a dragon’s teeth into that field, then beat the warriors who sprang up by tricking them into fighting each other
Orpheus drowned out the deadly song of the Sirens with his own music so the crew could sail past safely
After he left her for a Corinthian princess, Medea took revenge by killing their own two children
Years later in Corinth, abandoned Medea to marry the king’s daughter, Glauce (also called Creusa)
Fleeing Colchis with the stolen Fleece, Medea killed her own brother Apsyrtus to slow their pursuers
As a baby, was secretly raised by the wise centaur Chiron after Pelias seized his father’s throne
His ship was built by the craftsman Argus with help from the goddess Athena
The _Argo_ carried a magical speaking plank cut from Zeus’s sacred oak at Dodona
On the island of Lemnos, he and his crew were welcomed by Queen Hypsipyle and her husbandless subjects
His crew drove off the Harpies tormenting the blind prophet Phineus, who then gave them directions
Passed through the crashing Symplegades, or Clashing Rocks, by sending a dove through the gap first
At Colchis, the Fleece hung guarded by a dragon that never slept, until Medea sang it into slumber
Medea later tricked Pelias’s own daughters into killing him with a fake youth spell, falsely promising it would make him young again
In the best-known version of his death, the rotting _Argo_’s stern collapsed and killed him as he rested beneath it
After her revenge in Corinth, Medea escaped aboard a chariot lent by her grandfather, the sun god Helios

trap.title: Jason, or just an Argonaut?
trap.body: Clues about the crew—Heracles, Orpheus, Atalanta, the Sirens, Lemnos—describe the whole expedition, not Jason personally, so “Argonauts” or a crewmate’s name is a tempting but wrong early buzz. “Argo” is the ship, not its captain, and “Golden Fleece” is the prize he sought, not the hero himself.
trap.fix: Listen for what the pronoun is doing: a clue about leading, marrying Medea, or being sent by Pelias points to Jason specifically. A clue naming only another Argonaut’s deed (Heracles’s strength, Orpheus’s music) is not enough on its own to buzz “Jason.”
